task: As CTO of a 40-person startup, I need to tell everyone that the December offsite in Austin is cancelled because of budget cuts after our funding round came in smaller than planned. We're going to do a virtual holiday lunch instead and I want to acknowledge people were excited about it. Write the Slack announcement, about 150 words, direct but not cold.
rewrite:
ambition: A seasoned internal-comms lead would put the decision in the first line and own it in the CTO's voice ("we're cancelling," not "it has been decided"). They'd also name what's being lost (Austin, being together) instead of a generic "we know this is disappointing."

agency: The rawest material is the original offsite announcement and the team's reactions in Slack, plus whatever the CTO is willing to say about the funding round. None of it is in reach, so the draft uses only the stated facts, invents no figures, dates, or details, and leaves a blank for the lunch date and time.

acceleration: Use the standard bad-news structure: decision first, one plain sentence of reason, a specific acknowledgment, then what happens next. Format for Slack: short paragraphs, no headers or bullets, and at most one emoji, if any.

accuracy: Nothing outside the model can check tone. The closest proxy is the CTO, or the CEO or head of people, confirming that the stated reason matches what the company has already been told about the funding round.

deeper task:
Answer as an internal-communications lead at a startup who writes hard-news messages for founders. Your standard is that all 40 employees finish reading knowing what changed, why, and what happens next, and feel the CTO was straight with them.

Write a Slack announcement of about 150 words from the CTO to the whole company. The December offsite in Austin is cancelled because of budget cuts after the funding round came in smaller than planned. A virtual holiday lunch will take place instead. Acknowledge that people were excited about the offsite. The tone is direct but not cold. Lead with the cancellation, state the reason plainly without blaming anyone or over-explaining, and be specific about the disappointment. Don't invent figures, dates, perks, or details. Where a fact only the CTO knows is missing, such as the lunch date and time, leave a bracketed blank. The deliverable is only the message text, ready to paste into Slack, with no notes, options, or commentary.

answers.plain:
**Slack announcement:**

Hi team,

I have some disappointing news: we're cancelling the December offsite in Austin.

Our funding round came in smaller than we planned, and we're making budget cuts to extend our runway. The offsite was one of the things we had to give up. I know many of you were looking forward to it, and I was too. I wish I had better news.

To still mark the end of the year together, we'll hold a virtual holiday lunch in December. We'll cover the cost of your meal, and we'll set aside the time to catch up, celebrate what we've built this year, and have some fun. I'll share the date and details soon.

Thank you for your understanding, and for everything you've done this year. If you have questions or concerns, please reach out to me directly or bring them to our next all-hands. I'm happy to talk through any of it.

[Your name]

---

That's about 160 words. A few notes:

- I wrote that the company will cover meals for the lunch. That's an assumption, so change or remove it if it isn't the plan.
- I said you'll share details soon and mentioned the all-hands. Adjust these if the timing differs.
- If you'd like it to be more direct, cut "I wish I had better news" and the closing offer to talk.
answers.nudge:
**Slack announcement**

Hi all, I have some disappointing news: we're cancelling the December offsite in Austin.

Our funding round came in smaller than we planned, so we're cutting back on spending to protect our runway. The offsite was one of the things we had to cut. I know many of you were excited about it, and I was too. I didn't make this decision lightly.

Instead, we'll hold a virtual holiday lunch on [date] at [time]. [We'll cover a meal for everyone, so you can order something great wherever you are.] It won't be Austin, but I want it to be a real chance to celebrate the year together.

If you have questions about the decision, ask in this thread or grab time with me directly. I'll also cover it at the next all-hands.

Thank you for your understanding, and for everything you've put into this year.

**Notes**
- **Bracketed items:** Fill in the date and time. I added the meal line as a suggestion, so keep it only if you'll fund it. A stipend makes the lunch feel like a real replacement rather than a consolation prize.
- **Why the reason is stated plainly:** In a 40-person company, people will guess at the cause if you're vague, and the guesses are usually worse than the truth. "Smaller than planned" is honest without alarming anyone. If the runway line overstates things, change it to match your actual situation.
- **Before posting:** Tell your leadership team first so they can answer questions right away. Post it early in the week and in the morning, so people can react and ask questions during working hours.
answers.skill:
Team, the December offsite in Austin is cancelled.

Our funding round came in smaller than we planned, and we've had to cut the budget to match. The offsite was one of the things we couldn't keep.

I know many of you were looking forward to it. Getting everyone in one place, away from our screens, mattered to a lot of you, and I was looking forward to it too. This is a real disappointment, and I'm not going to pretend it isn't.

Instead, we'll hold a virtual holiday lunch on [date] at [time, time zone]. [One sentence on how the lunch will work, e.g. whether it's covered and how to join.] Calendar invites will go out by [date].

If you've already made travel or personal plans around the offsite, please message me directly at [contact method] so we can sort it out.

I'll share more on where the company stands at [meeting/date]. Questions are welcome in this thread or in a DM to me.

– [CTO name]
